rgb: This indoor dining scene places the camera wearer at a small, round, dark table located about 0.3 to 0.9 metres forward and below the viewpoint. A woman is seated opposite, approximately 0.8 to 1.0 metre away, while illuminated glass-door beverage coolers extend across the background at about 2.0 to 2.5 metres, roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres behind her. Dressed in a burgundy top and lanyard, she faces the camera wearer with her forearms crossed on the table's far edge, looking toward the wearer in frame 1 before her eyes become cropped. Several tabletop objects are within arm's reach of both people, at distances of 0.3 to 0.7 metres and spaced roughly 0.1 to 0.3 metres apart: a tall brown paper bag on the right, a green glass bottle immediately left of it, a white lidded cup directly behind the bottle near the woman's left arm, an orange candy pack at lower center, and foil-wrapped food in small white trays on the left and in the near foreground. The green bottle partly blocks the white cup and the woman's left forearm behind it, and the brown bag is partly cut off by the right edge. From left to right across all five frames, the people and table items stay fixed relative to one another as the wearer's head progressively pitches downward and tilts slightly left, causing the upper half of the woman's head to leave the top of the frame while additional tabletop area and foreground objects enter at the bottom.
depth: The depth map separates the view into four principal layers: the extremely bright brown paper bag at the far right, about 0.3–0.5 m away; the dark circular tabletop and its Perrier bottle, white disposable cup, wrapped food, and Reese's pack at roughly 0.4–0.9 m; the woman seated opposite at approximately 0.9–1.2 m, around 0.3–0.6 m behind the table objects; and the dark beverage coolers behind her at about 2.0–2.5 m. Every tabletop object and the paper bag is within arm's reach of both the woman and the camera wearer, and her folded arms lie directly along the table's far edge, just behind the cup and food container. The bag strongly blocks the table's right side in frame 1. From frames 1 through 5, the wearer moves while tilting downward and leftward, the bag withdraws toward the right boundary, and the foreground tabletop comes slightly closer; at the same time, the top of the woman's head is cropped by the upper edge beginning in frame 2. More clearly than the dim RGB view, the map displays both the continuous near-to-far gradient over the angled black tabletop and the precise separation between the bottle, cup, and woman's forearms. Its estimates are nevertheless unreliable on the background glass cooler doors, which collapse into an almost uniformly black void, and in frame 5, where motion blur makes the foreground bottle and paper-bag outlines bleed into the table.
segmentation: The segmentation view separates the foreground shapes and arrangement of objects on the table. It places the woman centrally, seated about 0.9–1.2 m ahead of the camera wearer with her torso facing forward, and identifies a green Perrier bottle around 0.5 m away at right-center, a white cup immediately behind and to the bottle's left at about 0.6 m, and a left-side food tray at roughly 0.7 m, all on the circular table and within reach of both people. Occlusion and incomplete visibility are represented throughout the sequence: in frames 1–4, the bottle overlaps both the cup and the woman's left arm, while the tall item along the right edge becomes narrower as the camera pans left and tilts downward from frames 1 to 5. Relative to the RGB strip by itself, the middle-frame masks make the precise pixel boundaries between the overlapping bottle, cup, and woman's dark sleeve on the dark tabletop immediately clear, and they even detect separate bottles inside the background cooler about 2 m away. Several masks and category assignments are highly unreliable, however. The brown paper bag on the right at approximately 0.4 m is incorrectly labelled as another "person" in frames 1–4; the background drink cooler is wrongly called a "tv" or "laptop"; the food container is misidentified as a "cup" in frame 2 and a "mouse" in frame 5; and both the Reese's wrapper and foreground tray go completely undetected in frame 5.
pose: The pose visualization follows the woman's 2D skeletal landmarks as she sits directly ahead of the camera wearer at about 0.9–1.2 m. It maps her shoulders, upper torso, elbows, and crossed wrists resting on the table within arm's reach, approximately 0.3–0.5 m, of the cup, bottle, and food objects. Her shoulder alignment and facial landmarks—eyes, nose, and ears detected in frames 1–4—face straight toward the camera wearer. Her head leans slightly to her right in frame 1, then becomes straighter and angles slightly downward while the camera view pitches down through frames 2–4. The table hides her lower body, and the upper image boundary progressively cuts off her head from frames 2 to 5, so the rendering contains only her upper-body skeleton plus a dense magenta grouping for her right hand placed over her left wrist. The map exposes the precise configuration of the crossed forearms, the elbow bends, and the finger joints of her right hand against her dark maroon sweater, details that merge together in the RGB images. The output is completely unreliable in frame 5, where no body or hand is detected after her head is fully cropped from view. It is also imperfect in frames 1–4 because her partly hidden left hand has no magenta hand skeleton, and an erroneous yellow lower-body landmark appears near the bottom of frame 4.
